name: Seotda
description: Seotda is a traditional Korean two-card game played with 20 Hwatu cards; players form ranked combinations (GwangTtaeng, Ttaeng, Geut) and bet. LA Seotda is a modern variant with a 52-card deck and poker-style elements.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: South Korea
Time Period: Traditional; Hwatu/Go-Stop culture
Historical Development: Traditional Korean two-card game played with 20 cards from a Hwatu deck (flower cards); combines luck and strategy with GwangTtaeng and Ttaeng hand rankings.
Cultural Significance: Popular social and gambling game in Korea; LA Seotda is a modern poker-influenced variant.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

rules.objective: Form the highest-ranking two-card hand (GwangTtaeng, Ttaeng, or Geut) to beat opponents and win the pot; players may fold to minimize losses.
rules.gameplay:
1. Card distribution: Each player is dealt two cards.
2. Betting rounds: After receiving cards, players in turn may Call (match the current bet), Raise (increase the bet), or Fold (drop out and forfeit stakes).
3. Showdown: After the final betting round, remaining players reveal their cards; the highest-ranking combination wins the pot.
keyRules: Hand rankings: GwangTtaeng (e.g. 3-8 Gwang) beats Ttaeng (pairs); Ttaeng beats Geut (sum of values, last digit); special hands 4-7 and 3-7 override certain combinations.
Betting: Call, Raise, or Fold each round; the best hand at showdown wins.
Traditional Seotda uses 20 Hwatu cards; LA Seotda uses a 52-card deck with poker-style bonuses (Ttaeng Value).

strategy.basic: Learn hand rankings (GwangTtaeng, Ttaeng, Geut, MangTong) and when to fold weak hands to limit losses.
strategy.intermediate: Bet early with strong hands (Ttaeng or higher) to pressure opponents; fold weak hands early; watch opponents' betting patterns to infer hand strength.
strategy.advanced: Know special hands (47 Amhaeng Eosa, 37 Ttaeng Jabi) and when they apply; balance bluffing with value betting; exploit opponents who call or raise too often.
tips: If your hand is weak, fold early to minimize losses.
With Ttaeng or higher, raise to pressure opponents.
Pay attention to opponents' betting patterns to read hand strength.

variations.name: LA Seotda
variations.description: Modern variant using a standard 52-card poker deck; adds Ttaeng Value (bonus winnings for strong hands like GwangTtaeng or Ttaeng) and poker-style hand rankings (e.g. Four of a Kind, Straight Flush).
